feature.title: Stabilize bassline and tempo tracking in visualizers
feature.request:
<task>
Resolve bassline, tempo and dancing tracking inconsistencies in visualizations
</task>

<context>
-If a song has a steady, uninterupted tempo, but additional notes are added in, the visualizers will react with a fast/slower tempo to try and match the temporary 'decorative' notes
</context>

<requirements>
-Use the new built-in debugger
-Use audio samples that ive gathered for you to test against (these samples have a steady tempo and the dancing-character visualization should be dancing at a consistent tempo for the whole trackso we should be testing on any deviations from it and devise a solution)
-Determine the cause of the inconsistencies
-Come up with a plan to resolve the inconsistencies and strengthen the audiovisualizer audio engine for future visualizations
</requirements>

<scope-and-non-goals>
-for now, we focus on only the bassline, but note other findings that may be causing awkwardness for future resolution
</scope-and-non-goals>

<verification>
-source of issue is identified. if not identified, establish leads and potential other causes
</verification>

problem.statement: On tracks with a constant tempo, added decorative notes make the visualizers react as if the tempo sped up or slowed down. The dancing character is the clearest case. Code reading points to six hypotheses, none measured yet. H1: the onset envelope scales the kick, mid and high bands each by its own recent peak and weights them equally (rhythmConfig.ts:40-44, rhythmAnalyzer.ts:118-123), so a quiet decoration gets as strong a vote as the kick. H2: each declared beat takes the strongest peak within +-0.2 of a period and moves phase by 0.4 and period by 0.1 of the error (beatTracker.ts:179-199), and that period is published directly as state.bpm (rhythmAnalyzer.ts:256), so at 120 BPM a single decoration can change the reported bpm by about 2 percent and the dance speed follows it (dancingCharacterSync.ts:165-168). H3: the tempo estimate can move to a faster pulse at half or a third of the lag when that peak scores 0.7 of the winner, and a challenger replaces the held tempo after 4 estimates, about 1 second (tempo.ts:175-191, rhythmConfig.ts:74-84); a move of more than 12 percent also rebuilds the beat grid (beatTracker.ts:87-90). H4: band-balance novelty or a 5 percent tempo jump held 3 seconds raises a soft song change (rhythmAnalyzer.ts:231-238, rhythmConfig.ts:168-171), which clears the dance lock and forgets the learned bassline (dancingCharacterSync.ts:136-140, dancingCharacterBassGate.ts:110-112). H5: the bass gate's bumps come from the beat clock rather than from kicks (dancingCharacterBassGate.ts:182-192), so any clock error reaches the bass pulse, and the kick band has no privileged role in setting that clock. H6: the dance also depends on tempoConfidence, meterConfidence and barPhase (dancingCharacterSync.ts:145-193, rhythmAnalyzer.ts:176-183), so a confidence dip or a downbeat correction can make the dancer jump with a perfectly steady bpm.
users: A listener watching dancing-character or another visualizer on a steady track
A developer building future visualizers on the shared audio and rhythm engine
evidence: User report: visualizers follow temporary decorative notes on a steady track
Code reading, verified by the lead: H1 to H5 in the problem statement, with file and line references
Telemetry gap: the dancing-character probe has no bpm, beat phase, beat count, song change or grid epoch columns (useDancingCharacterScene.ts:97), so the harness cannot yet measure tempo deviation
No harness run has been made: this planning session may not run it, so H1 to H5 are unmeasured hypotheses

goals: Establish by measurement which mechanisms cause tempo deviation on the samples in .debug-in, or record the remaining leads
Keep reported tempo and dance timing constant on constant-tempo tracks while decorative notes play
Make the same clip produce the same dance every time it is played
Make the bassline the anchor of the steady pulse in the shared engine, so every visualizer that reads it benefits
Give future visualizers a documented shared bass and beat surface instead of imports across visualizer folders
non_goals: Fixing mid or high band visual reactions; those findings are recorded for later
Following genuine mid-song tempo changes better than today; the user's samples all have a constant tempo
Improving meter (3 versus 4) detection or downbeat accuracy, beyond not regressing them
Upgrading three.js or changing dance animation clips
Shipping the debug harness to production
success_metrics: Tempo deviation on each .debug-in track after lock against its .bpm sidecar, measured before and after the fix, target within 1 percent
Count of false song changes and beat grid rebuilds per track, target zero
Share of post-lock time the dance lock and bass gate stay held, target above 99 percent
Spread across 4 runs of the same clip in chosen octave, beat times and dance position, target as in AC10
npm run eval:rhythm and the existing rhythm specs show no regression
constraints: Measurement uses npm run debug:viz and npm run debug:summary as documented in docs/agents/debug-harness.md
Harness additions stay DEV-only behind import.meta.env.DEV, and the production grep check in the harness doc stays clean
Bundle budgets in .size-limit.json may only be raised in the same PR with a stated reason (AGENTS.md); headroom was about 0.3 kB when the harness was frozen
No per-frame or per-audio-frame allocation; logic stays outside React; named exports only; 95 percent coverage

options.summary: Add DEV telemetry columns and a repeatability report, record a baseline, then apply the smallest in-place fixes (kick-weighted onset, bpm latch, boundary guard) chosen by which of H1-H5 the baseline confirms.
approach: S1 telemetry: extend the dancing-character DEV probe (useDancingCharacterScene.ts:97) with bpm, rawTempo, beatPhase, beatCount, songChangeCount, gridEpoch, timeScale, clipPhase; add a grid-epoch counter in beatTracker; extend debug:summary with per-window bpm deviation vs .bpm sidecar and event counts; all behind import.meta.env.DEV.

S2 baseline: run debug:viz 4x per .debug-in track on the unchanged tracker (fresh loads plus re-select); add a small repeatability script comparing octave, bpm, beat times, clip phase, lock time (AC10). Commit docs/agents/rhythm-findings.md marking H1-H5 confirmed/rejected/open, with other-band findings as later work (AC2, AC9).
S3 failing spec: synthetic constant-tempo signal with off-beat kick/mid/high decorations in the rhythmAnalyzer spec; must fail on the unchanged tracker (AC3).

S4 fixes only for confirmed hypotheses. H1: add per-band weights to rhythmConfig (kick high, mid/high low). H2: publish a slow-smoothed bpm (period gain 0.1 to about 0.02, phase gain kept) and freeze period inside a locked deadband. H3: raise the half/third takeover score threshold. H4: suppress soft boundaries while the tempo is locked and the jump is under the threshold. H5: gate bump clock locks to learned kick phase, not raw clock.
If measurement rejects a hypothesis, skip its fix and follow the next lead recorded in the findings; if none is confirmed, ship only S1-S3 and the findings (AC verification: leads established).
S5 move cubes/bassPulse.ts to app/features/audio/ and re-export nothing; update imports; add a short shared-surface section to docs/agents/architecture.md (AC7).
S6 re-record, run eval:rhythm before and after, check cubes and trio-color-wave in the harness, run all repo checks and size.

approach: S1 telemetry: extend devTelemetry/probes with bpm, rawTempo, beatPhase, beatCount, songChangeCount, gridEpoch, timeScale, clipPhase (DEV-only, preallocated); extend debug:summary with per-window deviation vs .bpm sidecar and event counts; add a repeatability report comparing 4 runs on track time (octave, bpm, beat times, clip phase, lock time) for AC10.

Baseline also shows run-to-run nondeterminism sources (AudioContext start offset, AGC warm-up, wall-clock vs track-time dt).
S3 failing spec: synthetic steady tempo plus off-beat decorations in kick/mid/high bands in testSignals; fails on the unchanged tracker (AC3).

S4 fixes, each shipped only if its hypothesis is confirmed: H1 kick-weighted onset (band weights in rhythmConfig, mid/high down-weighted, not removed); H2 publish a separately smoothed steady period (slow gain, outlier rejection of phase errors, deadband) instead of raw period as state.bpm; H3 require sustained evidence before subdivision takeover while locked; H4 raise soft-boundary evidence needed while locked, keep hard boundaries intact; H5 gate bump clock reads the steady pulse and kick evidence anchors phase.

If measurement rejects a hypothesis, drop its fix and pursue the next open lead from the findings doc; if all five are rejected, S4 is replaced by a new slice from the leads, and the failing spec is rewritten to the measured mechanism.
S5 determinism: make analysis advance on sample/track time, not wall clock; seed or reset AGC/gate/tracker state per track start; repeatability report becomes the AC10 check.

options.summary: Stop making the detector immune to decoration; add a separate latched 'steady pulse' layer in the shared engine that publishes a held tempo and a flywheel beat clock, anchored on kick-band evidence, and leaves the existing tracker untouched so eval:rhythm cannot regress.
approach: Slice 1 (all hypotheses): add DEV-only probe columns (bpm, rawTempo, beatPhase, beatCount, songChangeCount, gridEpoch, timeScale, clipPhase), extend debug:summary with per-window deviation vs .bpm, run the harness 4x per .debug-in clip, commit baseline findings (AC1, AC2, AC10 report).

Breaks the assumption that the tracker's per-beat period must be the published tempo: add SteadyPulse that consumes tracker output (rawTempo, beat events) plus a kick-only onset tap and publishes bpm only from a heavily averaged, latched estimate.

Latch: after lock, hold the tempo; release only when the raw estimate disagrees by >5% for several seconds AND kick-band support agrees. Phase runs as a flywheel with tiny kick-weighted corrections (replacing H2 gain 0.4/0.1 for consumers).

Boundary guard: SteadyPulse ignores soft song changes unless the latched tempo is also rejected; hard (silence) boundaries still reset it. Dancing-character reads SteadyPulse, so decoration-driven soft resets no longer clear the dance lock.
Repeatability: SteadyPulse is a pure function of track-time onsets, with no wall-clock or random state, resets fully on source change, and the harness report compares 4 runs (AC10).

If measurement rejects H1/H3, drop the kick-only tap and latch only the period; if H4 is rejected, drop the boundary guard; if H2 is rejected, shrink to a tempo latch; if H5 is confirmed, drive bass bumps from the flywheel plus kicks.
Move the bass/beat surface to app/features/rhythm/steadyPulse and document it in architecture.md (AC7); verify cubes and trio-color-wave in the harness.

decision_rationale: O1 scores highest because it is cheap and fits as is, but it leaves repeatability (D8) unplanned and makes the bass only a weight, which misses the anchor goal. O2 covers those at the highest cost and adds a facade plus a second state field. O3 leaves two tempo sources and does not meet AC3 as worded. O4 takes O1's in-place fixes, O3's flywheel inside the analyzer so one tempo source remains, and O2's repeatability work. Its slices are gated, so if the baseline rejects a hypothesis the work shrinks towards O1.

design.overview: Measure first. Telemetry and reports make tempo deviation and repeatability visible, and the baseline records which hypotheses hold; later slices are confirmed or dropped against those findings. Input causes come first, because a held clock fed a bad estimate would latch it: onset band weights (H1), faster-pulse takeover while locked (H3), soft boundaries while the tempo is still supported (H4), and confidence or bar phase jumps (H6). If the findings still show beat-level wobble (H2, H5), the published clock is separated from the raw detector: BeatTracker keeps detecting, and a pure steady clock owned by RhythmAnalyzer turns its beats into state.bpm and beatPhase. After lock, its period is averaged from measured beat intervals rather than copied from the tempo estimate, which is limited by lag bins of about 2 percent at 120 BPM; it uses a deadband of 0.3 percent, well inside the 1 percent tolerance. Phase corrections are small, favour kick-band evidence and ignore outliers, so kick-band decorations are covered as well as mid and high ones. The bass gate keeps its clock-driven bumps, which become steady once the clock is. Code check: cubes reads downbeatCount and RhythmStats reads bpm and beatPhase, so the change reaches them, and the context brief's statement that only dancing-character reads rhythm state is wrong. trio-color-wave was not seen reading rhythm state in the search, and the final slice confirms this.

contracts.name: Telemetry columns
contracts.definition: The dancing-character probe adds bpm, rawBeatBpm, rawTempoBpm, tempoConfidence, meterConfidence, beatsPerBar, beatPhase, barPhase, beatCount, songChanges, gridEpoch, timeScale, clipPhase, phaseNudge, meterLocked, bumpCount and kickPhaseOffset (the latest kick's phase minus the learned kick place). This changes the frozen C2 contract in docs/agents/debug-harness.md, so the doc and every consumer change together. Values are read through existing or minimal read-only accessors, and any production delta is measured with npm run size.

contracts.name: Report commands
contracts.definition: npm run debug:summary reads a sidecar named after the track and prints per-window bpm deviation and event counts. A new repeatability command takes 2 or more telemetry CSVs and prints the AC10 comparison on track time. Beat times are computed from t and beatPhase rather than from counter changes, so frame rate does not limit their accuracy. Both are pure functions over parsed tables.

contracts.name: RhythmState meaning
contracts.definition: Fields and types stay the same. If the steady clock ships, state.bpm and state.beatPhase become its output once a beat is locked, and barPhase is anchored to the same clock. Its period is averaged from measured beat intervals with a 0.3 percent deadband. Published phase never steps by more than 0.02 of a beat per declared beat, apart from a grid rebuild or a reset. Raw values stay internal to the analyzer. Hard resets clear the clock, and real song changes still release it.

contracts.name: Shared bass and beat surface
contracts.definition: BassPulse and the bass gate are exported from app/features/rhythm with behaviour unchanged by the move and covered by their existing specs, which move with them. docs/agents/architecture.md documents them with useRhythm and tracker.state. No visualizer imports bass or beat code from another visualizer's folder.

design.data: No persisted data. Telemetry stays in git-ignored .debug-out. Sample audio stays in .debug-in; whether it is committed is the user's call.
design.ux: Viewers should see a dance and bass pulse that hold steady through decorations and repeat from run to run. The on-screen BPM readout in RhythmStats also stops wobbling. No new controls.
design.accessibility: No UI changes. Existing axe checks in e2e still apply.
design.security_privacy: Everything stays client-side. Harness code stays DEV-only, and no audio leaves the machine.
design.observability: The harness is the observability tool: per-window deviation, event counts and the repeatability report, recorded in the findings document before and after each fix.
design.rollout: One pull request per slice, using Conventional Commit titles; any change under app/ needs a releasing type. Cloudflare previews each PR and deploys main. S1 to S4 do not change production behaviour. S3 is a review point where the user confirms which of S5, S6 and S7 proceed, their size and the AC10 targets. Each PR that grows the bundle states its size delta, and any budget raise is made in that same PR. Rollback is a Cloudflare rollback or a revert of that slice.

test_strategy.unit: Pure specs for the steady clock, onset weighting, boundary guard and report functions. Decoration signals are added to testSignals.ts covering off-beat notes in the kick, mid and high bands, plus a tempo that falls between lag bins, a kickless signal and a crossfade fixture. The new spec is recorded as it.fails on the unchanged tracker and .fails is removed by the fix. A spec asserts the phase step limit in C3 and that the gate stays open on the decoration signal.
test_strategy.integration: RhythmAnalyzer spec runs decoration signals end to end. Existing boundary and meter specs stay green. npm run eval:rhythm runs before and after on the datasets named in the findings, including .debug-in WAVs with sidecars, as a fast offline check.
test_strategy.e2e: npm run test:e2e after build. Existing specs cover rendering, context release and no console errors.
test_strategy.manual: npm run debug:viz on each .debug-in track 4 times with dancing-character, in fresh loads and by re-selecting in one page, plus cubes and trio-color-wave once after the clock or input fixes and again at the end. Watch the dancer in npm run dev, because the numbers cannot show whether it looks right.
test_strategy.non_functional: npm run size, the production grep from the harness doc, no per-frame allocation, and fps above the harness's 50 fps reliability floor for any run counted as evidence.

open_questions.question: Should cubes and trio-color-wave later adopt the steady beat for their bass reactions? They keep their own BassPulse-style reaction in this work.
After the baseline, do the AC10 repeatability numbers need adjusting? Answered at the S3 review, before S7 starts.
AGENTS.md says rhythm specs use it.fails, but none exist in app/. Correct the doc in S4 when the new it.fails spec lands?
What is the true tempo of each .debug-in sample? A .bpm sidecar per track is needed before the S3 baseline.

findings.finding: AC1, AC4, D7 and the first success metric all measure against a .bpm sidecar, but .debug-in holds only 'Untitled Bounce.wav' and no slice creates or requests the sidecar. No slice says what happens when a track has no sidecar. The sidecar value is also one octave-ambiguous number, while the dance normalizes octave on its own (dancingCharacterSync.ts:165), so 'within 1 percent' needs an octave rule that the plan does not give.
findings.suggestion: Add to S1 an explicit prerequisite: the user supplies a .bpm file per track (the plan owner asks for it now). Define the comparison as octave-normalized to the sidecar. Define the behaviour when no sidecar exists (report only, no pass/fail). Mark AC4 not evaluable until it exists.
findings.resolution: Changed: AC1 and AC4 are octave-normalized, a missing sidecar is report-only, Q4 and K8 ask Trevor for sidecars before the baseline.

findings.finding: S4 (the L, R2 steady clock) is built unconditionally before S5 (the input fixes), although S5 is the only slice gated on which hypotheses the baseline confirms. S4 lists AC4 and AC5 as acceptance, but those depend on tempo input quality (H1, H3) and on false soft song changes (H4), which are fixed in S5. A held clock fed a corrupted or wrong-octave estimate latches it (K3 says so), so S4 cannot honestly meet AC4/AC5 alone if the baseline shows H1/H3/H4 dominate. S4's draft_paths also omit boundary.ts and dancingCharacterSync.ts, which H4 needs for AC5.
findings.suggestion: Gate S4 on the S2 findings like S5, and order input-side fixes before the clock, or make S4 acceptance only AC3 on its own signal and move AC4/AC5 to the end of S5. State in S2 which findings would make the clock unnecessary.
findings.resolution: Changed: input fixes now come before the clock, and the clock is conditional on re-measured findings. Draft paths include boundary.ts and dancingCharacterSync.ts.

findings.finding: The design sets a 1 percent deadband on the held period while D6/AC4 allow exactly 1 percent deviation. A period that sits at the deadband edge is a pass or fail by rounding, so the held tempo has no margin. HOP_SECONDS is 0.01 (rhythmConfig.ts:10), so one autocorrelation lag bin is about 2 percent at 120 BPM. If the held period is seeded from the tempo estimate rather than from averaged beat intervals, 1 percent is not reachable even with a perfect hold. The plan does not say what feeds the held period.
findings.suggestion: Set the deadband well under the tolerance (for example 0.3 percent) and in C3 state that the held period is averaged from measured beat intervals (sub-bin), not copied from the quantized tempo estimate. Add a spec for a true tempo that falls between lag bins.
findings.resolution: Changed: deadband is 0.3 percent, the period is averaged from measured beat intervals, and AC3 includes a tempo between lag bins.

findings.finding: The dance does not only follow state.bpm. computeDanceTiming (dancingCharacterSync.ts:145-193) also locks and unlocks on tempoConfidence, enters meter lock on meterConfidence, and nudges clip position from barPhase when the bar is 4 beats, using rhythm.barPhase derived from meter.barPosition(anchorBeatIndex) (rhythmAnalyzer.ts:177-183). C3 steadies only bpm and beatPhase, and the C1 columns omit tempoConfidence, meterConfidence, barPhase and the meterLocked/barLocked states. A downbeat correction or meter shrink can shift barPhase and make the dancer jump with a perfectly steady bpm. This is an unlisted candidate cause (a sixth hypothesis) that the baseline cannot see.
findings.suggestion: Add tempoConfidence, meterConfidence, beatsPerBar, barPhase, meterLocked and the phase nudge to C1 and AC1. Add H6 'bar phase or confidence jumps' to the findings table and say in C3 whether barPhase is anchored to the steady clock.
findings.resolution: Changed: H6 added, C1 gained the confidence, bar and nudge columns, and C3 anchors barPhase to the clock.

findings.finding: Size budget handling is placed too late. Headroom is about 0.3 kB, S1 adds production-visible accessors and S4 adds steadyClock.ts to the entry bundle, but only S7 lists .size-limit.json in its draft_paths. K6 says the raise happens in the same PR as the cause, and CI size would fail the S4 PR (one PR per slice per the rollout). The plan also never says which budget (entry 133 kB, total 312 kB) is at risk.
findings.suggestion: Put .size-limit.json in S1 and S4 draft_paths, record the size before S1 as the gate in S1, and decide in S2 whether S4 needs a raise with the stated reason.
findings.resolution: Changed: S2 records sizes, .size-limit.json is in the S2 and S6 draft paths, and any raise lands in the PR that causes it.

findings.finding: Contract gap on phase between the flywheel and the bass gate. dancingCharacterBassGate.ts:158 reads rhythm.beatPhase to learn the kick phase and closes the gate on off-phase kicks. C3 says the clock makes small, kick-favoured phase corrections and ignores outliers, and C4 says the gate keeps its current behaviour. If the clock slews slowly, a steady offset from the true kick phase makes the gate see kicks as off-phase and close, which is the reverse of AC5. The plan gives no spec or telemetry for the offset between the published phase and the kick onsets, and updatePhase extrapolates from anchorTime/anchorPeriod so changing those on each beat can also step the phase.
findings.suggestion: Add a continuity requirement to C3 (published phase never steps by more than a stated fraction per beat) and a spec that the gate stays open on the AC3 signal. Add a 'kick minus beat phase' telemetry column.
findings.resolution: Changed: C3 limits phase steps to 0.02 of a beat, kickPhaseOffset is a column, and AC3 requires the gate to stay open.

findings.finding: AC5 is not observable as written. 'Bass bumps stay evenly spaced' has no threshold and no telemetry column for bump times (C1 lists none), and 'post-lock time' is not defined (which lock: tempoLocked in the probe, beat.locked, or the first beat). AC3 also says the spec 'fails on the unchanged tracker', but nothing says what to do if hand-built synthetic decorations do not reproduce the real-file deviation (the spec passes on the old code), so the spec could be green and meaningless.
findings.suggestion: Define post-lock as tempoLocked first held for 2 s, add a bump-time column and a spacing threshold (for example inter-bump interval within 10 percent of the beat period). In S3 require the decoration parameters to be fitted to the S2 deviations; if the spec cannot fail, record that as a finding rather than weakening the spec.
findings.resolution: Changed: AC5 defines post-lock and a bump spacing threshold, bumpCount is a column, AC3 uses fitted signals and records a failure to reproduce as a finding.

findings.finding: S6 (AC10 repeatability) is an open-ended 'remove the causes the report finds' slice sized M, dependent only on S4, with draft_paths of the whole app/features/rhythm/ folder. Known candidates from the plan itself (AudioContext start offset, AGC warm-up, wall-clock vs track time, state carried over when re-selecting in one page) can each touch the audio engine, not just rhythm. AC10 numbers (40 ms, 5 percent of a loop, 2 s lock spread) are a planner-assumption (D9) with analysis already about 100 ms behind real time, and the plan treats them as pass/fail ACs while K7 admits they may be unreachable. Q2 is non-blocking though S6 cannot finish without an answer.
findings.suggestion: Make S6 conditional on the S2 repeatability results, size it after S2, and make Q2 blocking at the S2 review point. Treat AC10 as a measured target set from the baseline, not a fixed gate, until then.
findings.resolution: Changed: S7 is conditional and sized at the S3 review, AC10 targets are confirmed there, and its paths include the audio engine. Q2 stays non-blocking because the plan answers it at that review.

findings.finding: AC6 and the regression metric rely on 'any dataset run before and after' with npm run eval:rhythm, but the plan does not say which labelled datasets exist in the repo or on the user's machine. If the only labelled data is the one .debug-in file, eval:rhythm cannot detect the kickless-music regression named in K5 or the slower new-tempo reporting in K4. The 'no later than today' crossfade criterion has no named test fixture either.
findings.suggestion: State in S1 which datasets eval:rhythm will run on, and add synthetic kickless and crossfade fixtures in testSignals.ts (the file already builds tempo ramps) as part of S3 so K4 and K5 have a regression test.
findings.resolution: Changed: findings must name the eval datasets, and S4 adds kickless and crossfade fixtures named in AC6.

findings.finding: C3 changes the meaning of state.bpm and beatPhase for every reader, including the on-screen RhythmStats readout and cubes' downbeatCount (stated in the design), yet only S7 checks other visualizers, after all behaviour changes have merged. The move of bassPulse and the gate (S7) comes after S4-S6 edit the same area, creating avoidable merge churn, and C4 'current behaviour' is not tested by any named spec.
findings.suggestion: Do the file move first (a pure rename PR, no behaviour change) or fold it into S1, and run cubes and trio-color-wave in the harness at the end of S4 as well.
findings.resolution: Changed: the pure rename is now S1, and cubes and trio-color-wave are checked in S6 and S8.

freeze_first.name: Shared bass and beat surface
freeze_first.definition: BassPulse and the bass gate are exported from app/features/rhythm with behaviour unchanged by the move and covered by their existing specs, which move with them. docs/agents/architecture.md documents them with useRhythm and tracker.state. No visualizer imports bass or beat code from another visualizer's folder.

freeze_first.name: Telemetry columns
freeze_first.definition: The dancing-character probe adds bpm, rawBeatBpm, rawTempoBpm, tempoConfidence, meterConfidence, beatsPerBar, beatPhase, barPhase, beatCount, songChanges, gridEpoch, timeScale, clipPhase, phaseNudge, meterLocked, bumpCount and kickPhaseOffset (the latest kick's phase minus the learned kick place). This changes the frozen C2 contract in docs/agents/debug-harness.md, so the doc and every consumer change together. Values are read through existing or minimal read-only accessors, and any production delta is measured with npm run size.

freeze_first.name: Report commands
freeze_first.definition: npm run debug:summary reads a sidecar named after the track and prints per-window bpm deviation and event counts. A new repeatability command takes 2 or more telemetry CSVs and prints the AC10 comparison on track time. Beat times are computed from t and beatPhase rather than from counter changes, so frame rate does not limit their accuracy. Both are pure functions over parsed tables.

freeze_first.name: RhythmState meaning
freeze_first.definition: Fields and types stay the same. If the steady clock ships, state.bpm and state.beatPhase become its output once a beat is locked, and barPhase is anchored to the same clock. Its period is averaged from measured beat intervals with a 0.3 percent deadband. Published phase never steps by more than 0.02 of a beat per declared beat, apart from a grid rebuild or a reset. Raw values stay internal to the analyzer. Hard resets clear the clock, and real song changes still release it.
